'''Bruce George Lindsay''' (March 7, 1947 – May 5, 2015) was an American [[statistician]] best known for his contributions to [[mixture model]]ing and [[Likelihood function|likelihood theory]].

==Biography==
Lindsay was born in 1947 in [[The Dalles]], [[Oregon]]. He earned a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in [[mathematics]] from the [[University of Oregon]] in 1969 and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[biomathematics]] from the [[University of Washington]] in 1978.<ref name="CV-BGL">{{Cite web |url=https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/13856481/CV-BGL.pdf |title=Bruce G. Lindsay -- CV February 2015 |access-date=2015-05-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304074623/https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/13856481/CV-BGL.pdf |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Between his undergraduate and graduate studies he has served in the [[U.S. Coast Guard]] for four years during the [[Vietnam War]].<ref>[http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/centredaily/obituary.aspx?n=bruce-lindsay&pid=174827304&fhid=15341  Centre Daily Times obituary, May 10, 2015]</ref> He joined the [[Pennsylvania State University]] faculty in 1979, heading the Department of Statistics in 1998–2000 and 2006–2012 and rising to the rank of Eberly Chair in Statistics in 2012.<ref name="CV-BGL" /> He was also a visiting professor at the [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1987, the [[Yale University]] in 1990, and [[North Carolina State University]] in 2004–2005.<ref name="CV-BGL" /> He was elected to be a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1987, of the [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|Guggenheim Foundation]] in 1996, and of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1998.<ref name="CV-BGL" />

==Selected publications==
* Lindsay, Bruce G. "Mixture models: theory, geometry and applications." NSF-CBMS regional conference series in probability and statistics. Institute of Mathematical Statistics and the American Statistical Association, 1995.
* Lindsay, Bruce G. "The geometry of mixture likelihoods: a general theory." The Annals of Statistics 11.1 (1983): 86–94.
* Lindsay, Bruce G. "Composite likelihood methods." Contemporary Mathematics 80.1 (1988): 221–39.
* Lindsay, Bruce G. "Efficiency versus robustness: the case for minimum Hellinger distance and related methods." The Annals of Statistics 22.2 (1994): 1081–1114.
* Lindsay, Bruce G. "The geometry of mixture likelihoods, part II: the exponential family." The Annals of Statistics 11.3 (1983): 783–792.
